correctness.rationale: The exact conditional jump moment is sum |b_i|^q r_i^(beta-q)/sum r_j^beta; Gaussian radius local density r^(d-1), max-radius sector decomposition, and sharp lower cone bounds give finite iff q<min(md,d+beta) including both equality divergences. State-independent projection norm<=1 proves finite-time sufficiency; bounded-prestate and unbounded jump moments prove necessity. Full support of the selected Gaussian direction makes E||Bv||^q uniformly contracting on the unit sphere; W1 contraction and Lq bounds establish unique invariant law and its exact moment spectrum, including the d=1 reset exception. In centered beta=2 case, Gamma/Dirichlet factorization proves exact one-step q formula and orthogonality yields the q=2 recurrence. The actual standalone verifier completed exact gamma-ratio and independently simulated checks. Independent auditing is not claimed.

value.rationale: The precise integrability threshold governs which expected powers of iterate error and stationary noise floor are mathematically meaningful for noisy numerical row actions. It separates two distinct structural failure mechanisms: an individual selected near-zero row, mitigated by norm-power sampling, versus near-simultaneous collapse of all candidate rows, which cannot be mitigated by any such sampling exponent. For example in scalar Kaczmarz, ordinary squared-norm sampling restores finite variance with three candidate rows while uniform sampling never does, but still leaves an infinite third moment. The exact centered q=2 recursion and equilibrium floor make the distinction operationally interpretable and not a mere restatement of an inverse-Gaussian moment.
